title: Adic proper adjunction comparison on the two constructible localizing presentations
statement:
Fix a universe $u$, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes in universe $u$, and let $g:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate] of one of the families $\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure convention [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\mathcal B_T\subset D_T$ be the bounded constructible object property of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with constructibility in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense [def-sfb-constructible-module], and let $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ use finite constant local models and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Form $\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ and $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal C_T)$ by [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure; sk-def-localizing-closure], in the same ordinary $D_T$ and with the same ambient coproducts indexed in universe $u+1$.

Then $\mathcal B_T=\mathcal C_T$ and $\mathcal L_T=\mathcal H_T$ as object properties in $D_T$. These identifications preserve the full inclusions into $D_T$ and the inclusions of the bounded subcategories into their hulls.

Let $F_g:\mathcal L_Z\to\mathcal L_Y$ be the canonical restriction of the actual ambient $Rg_*$ [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward]. Given a compact-support adjunction $a:Rg_!\dashv J$ on $\mathcal H_Z,\mathcal H_Y$ as in [sk-prop-sf-existence], the proper compactification comparison gives a natural isomorphism $e:Rg_!\xrightarrow{\sim}F_g$ under the displayed hull identifications. On $\mathcal L_Z,\mathcal L_Y$ it induces an adjunction $F_g\dashv J$ whose natural Hom bijection, for $M\in\mathcal L_Z$, $N\in\mathcal L_Y$ and $h:F_gM\to N$, is $h\longmapsto a_{M,N}(h\circ e_M)$. No derived-completeness condition is imposed.
